## Summary

I implemented upstream-basename-preserving tarball routing across four source files (no test files touched).

**`pnpr/crates/pnpr/src/upstream.rs`**
- Added `pub fn tarball_basename(url: &str) -> Option<&str>` — cuts the string at the first `?` or `#`, takes the last `/`-segment, and returns `None` for an empty segment (trailing slash). Borrows from the input, so bare relative names work too. Verified against all five contract examples.
- Added `pub fn rewritten_tarball_basename(manifest, pkg, map_key)` — the single source of truth for the basename pnpr advertises: the upstream `dist.tarball` basename when usable, else the conventional `<name>-<version>.tgz` keyed off the manifest's declared `version` field (falling back to the map key).
- `rewrite_dist_tarball` now uses that helper, so the rewritten URL preserves the upstream basename verbatim (including non-canonical names) and strips query/fragment, while still pointing back through the proxy.

**`pnpr/crates/pnpr/src/server.rs`** (`serve_tarball`)
- Normalizes the request to a bare, path-safe basename (also strips the decoded `@scope/` component of the libnpmpublish wire form and neutralizes traversal).
- Resolves the served version by matching the basename against each version's advertised basename (`resolve_tarball_route`), rather than parsing a version out of the filename — so integrity, OSV screening, upstream fetch path, and cache key are all bound to the *declaring* version.
- A basename claimed by two versions returns the new `AmbiguousTarball` error (502) **before** any upstream tarball fetch — only the packument is fetched.
- Kept the hosted-store open ahead of the packument load, preserving the fail-closed security property.

**`pnpr/crates/pnpr/src/package_name.rs`** — added `pub fn is_safe_tarball_filename` (path-safety without requiring the `<name>-<version>.tgz` convention).

**`pnpr/crates/pnpr/src/error.rs`** — added the `AmbiguousTarball` variant mapped to `502 Bad Gateway`.
